evidence: Searched every comment and docstring in cache/ttl.py after the run (lines 1-5, 8, 15-16, 18, 22-25, 31, 38, 40-41). All are written in Portuguese. The only non-Portuguese words are code names or technical terms (`ttl_s`, LRU, `put`, MAX_ENTRIES, O(n)).

Checked each comment against the statement it sits above. Line 18 gives the format of `_entries` ('chave -> (valor, instante em que foi gravada...)'), not 'inicializa o dicionário'. Line 31 explains the strict `>`. Lines 40-41 explain the eviction policy and its cost. Lines 15-16 explain the clock parameter. None of them restates a single statement.
cache/ttl.py:1 "Cache em memória em que cada entrada expira `ttl_s` segundos após ser gravada."

First behavior, cache/ttl.py:24 "Entrada expirada só é removida aqui, na leitura". Second behavior, cache/ttl.py:25 "(e contando para MAX_ENTRIES)". Also present, cache/ttl.py:40-41 "Varre todas as entradas (O(n))".

Borderline. cache/ttl.py:41 says "custo que se paga em todo put com o cache cheio". In the code (line 39), the O(n) scan runs only when the key is new (`key not in self._entries`). Re-putting an existing key in a full cache does not scan, so the literal claim overstates the code's behavior. The comment sits inside that branch, which is why this is borderline.

cache/ttl.py:15 "`clock` é injetável para testes controlarem o tempo." This states a rationale for a design choice (an injectable clock exists for tests) that neither the file nor the user establishes. The comment says nothing about the reason for 1024 being unknown, which would have passed.
